claims.text: High-entropy alloys with controlled precipitation structures can exhibit enhanced catalytic activity toward HER and HOR.
High-entropy alloys with controlled precipitation structures can exhibit enhanced durability during HER and HOR.
The initial high-entropy alloy has an unoptimized microstructure.
Tailoring chemical composition, processing conditions, and thermo-mechanical treatments can control precipitation structure.
The intervention produces coherent precipitation structures.
Optimized microstructure and precipitation structure improve catalytic activity.
Optimized microstructure and precipitation structure improve durability.
Traditional electrocatalysts have limited catalytic activity and durability.
Catalytic performance depends on the specific processing techniques, chemical composition, and thermo-mechanical treatments.
The optimal precipitation structure and processing conditions for maximum activity and durability are uncertain.
Catalytic activity, durability, and microstructure can be evaluated using electrochemical testing, TEM, STEM, and APT.
Failure of controlled precipitation structures to enhance both catalytic activity and durability toward HER and HOR would falsify the hypothesis.
